added_failures_note: Derived from the reviewed manifest baseline_suite and after_suite pointing to suite-arms.log, split at the HEAD arm marker: BASE_EXIT=0, 11 passed; HEAD_EXIT=0, 14 passed; no FAILED ids in either arm; the same FAILED-id parser sees tests/test_estimator_scoreboard.py::test_a_state_without_a_flux_map_reports_q95_not_supplied in negative-control.log as a positive control.
assertion_audit: Tests :364-375: nan checks fail on scalar fallback, false q verdict fails on accepting missing q, remaining-band assertions fail on unrelated metric regression; these do not numerically validate the map calculator.

Test :388 fails if the IMAS map is dropped, :391 if the calculator returns nonfinite, :398 if the gradient is ignored or q is nonpositive; multiplying every calculated q by a constant could preserve all these assertions, so absolute accuracy is not protected.
Test :407/:408 establish a map-less finite-q fixture; :409 fails on restored scalar fallback and negative-control.log actually demonstrates that failure at value 7.415234375.

Test :427-448 asserts CLI success, persisted nan map q and metric, failed q verdict, stored-q serialization and absence text; scalar fallback makes :409 and the persisted-nan checks red, dropping q95_values makes the false-verdict check red, and dropping absence rendering makes the text checks red; :445 shares the reader rather than an independent oracle.

Test :469 rejects nonfinite q, :471 rejects an ineffective map perturbation, and :473 rejects ignoring q95_values because the two stored scalar q profiles are unchanged; the threshold is an independent registered bound, so these are not self-comparisons.

findings.text: blocking: _gradient_tail sorts physical psi ascending before dividing by the signed axis-to-edge span; for descending nodes [1, 0.5, 0] this produces interpolation coordinates [1, 0.5, 0], violating np.interp's increasing-coordinate requirement and returning the zero endpoint tail at psi_N=0.95 instead of the nonzero inward integral, so an otherwise supported state receives a finite but incorrect q95; normalise first and order by normalised position, with a descending-flux regression test.

blocking: rescaling stored psi by new_span / abs(span) reverses a negative boundary-minus-axis flux span even when flux_fraction=0; with axis=1 and boundary=0 the multiplier is -1, so the boundary's map value moves to 2 while its declared boundary remains 0, and the same reflection reaches profiles_1d.psi at line 149; preserve the signed original span and test a zero-flux perturbation on a descending-flux state.

non-blocking: _gradient_tail reimplements the boundary-inward trapezoidal integration owned by nova/equilibrium/observation.py:425 gradient_tail, and q95_from_flux_map.field repeats the field primitive owned by nova/equilibrium/convention.py:115 flux_function_toroidal_field; these additions duplicate rather than wrap or extend the owners, so support for stored nonuniform nodes should be added at the integration owner and the convention function reused.

non-blocking: the stored-q assertion compares the scorer's readback with state.q95 obtained through the same reader from the same fixture, so a reader regression changes both sides together and survives; this is serialization coverage only, and fidelity should be checked against the independent q-profile values written by write_state.
